There was in the gallery a kind of stillness that did not forbid speech so much as embarrass it. Helena entered with the key hidden in her glove, as though secrecy might be made elegant by good breeding. Portraits watched from their frames with the tired tolerance of relations who have witnessed too many family recoveries. The dust had been disturbed in a single path, and she disliked that evidence of purpose more than she could have disliked open disorder. A gentleman may leave confusion behind him, she thought, but purpose leaves a signature. She bent near a cabinet, found it locked, and felt the smallest rise of temper, which in her was always the beginning of clarity. The windows admitted a thin light that spared nothing. It showed the crack in the lacquer, the bent corner of a catalogue, and the unsteady line of footprints that led toward a curtain nobody had thought worth replacing.
